celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ﴾ — for clarification (bayān) — ﴿أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, that is, the idol-worshippers; conjoined to «أهل». ﴿مُنْفَكِّينَ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «يكن», that is, leaving what they were upon, ﴿حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾, that is, came to them ﴿الْبَيِّنَةُ﴾, that is, the clear proof, which is Muhammad ﷺ:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: a badal (substitute) from «البينة», and he is the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿يَتْلُوا صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً﴾ from falsehood,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فِيهَا كُتُبٌ﴾: written rulings ﴿قَيِّمَةٌ﴾: upright; that is, he recites the content of that, which is the Qur'an. Some of them believed in it and some of them disbelieved.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ concerning belief in him ﴿إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ﴾, that is, he ﷺ, or the Qur'an that he brought as a miracle for him. Before his ﷺ coming they were united in believing in him when he would come; then those of them who disbelieved in him envied him.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَمَا أُمِرُوا﴾ in their two books, the Torah and the Gospel, ﴿إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾, that is, «أن يعبدوه» ("that they worship Him"): «أن» was dropped and the lām added; ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ from associating partners, ﴿حُنَفَاءَ﴾: steadfast on the religion of Ibrāhīm and the religion of Muhammad when he would come — so how did they disbelieve in him? — ﴿وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَوةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ﴾ the creed ﴿الْقَيِّمَةِ﴾: the upright.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾: an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), that is, their eternity in it having been decreed by Allah the Exalted. ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ﴾

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ﴾: creation.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿جَزَاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾: of abiding ﴿تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ through their obedience to Him ﴿وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ with His reward. ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ﴾: feared His punishment and so refrained from disobeying Him, Exalted is He.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam; ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: the noun of yakun; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: conjoined to أهل; ﴿مُنْفَكِّينَ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of yakun; ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and of the genitive; ﴿تَأْتِيَهُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after ḥattā, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْبَيِّنَةُ﴾: agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to منفكين.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾: badal (substitute) for البينة; ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) رسول; ﴿يَتْلُوا﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿صُحُفاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مُطَهَّرَةً﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is an adjective of رسول.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿فِيها﴾: the preposition and its genitive noun are the fronted khabar (predicate); ﴿كُتُبٌ﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿قَيِّمَةٌ﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is an adjective of صحفا.

daas-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.
﴿أُوتُوا﴾: a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تفرق; ﴿ما جاءَتْهُمُ﴾: ما is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and a past verb and its object; ﴿الْبَيِّنَةُ﴾: agent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿أُمِرُوا﴾: a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿لِيَعْبُدُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of reason (taʿlīl), the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أمروا; ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾: ḥāl; ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to what precedes them; ﴿الدِّينَ﴾: direct object of the active participle مخلصين; ﴿حُنَفاءَ﴾: a second ḥāl; ﴿وَيُقِيمُوا﴾: conjoined to يعبدوا, accusative like it; ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾: direct object; ﴿وَيُؤْتُوا﴾: also conjoined to يعبدوا, accusative like it; ﴿الزَّكاةَ﴾: direct object. ﴿وَذلِكَ دِينُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); ﴿الْقَيِّمَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِي نارِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: ḥāl; ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to what precedes them. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿هُمْ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ﴾: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, muḍāf to البرية; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿هُمْ﴾: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); ﴿خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, muḍāf to البرية; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause إن الذين… is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿جَزاؤُهُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾: khabar (predicate), muḍāf to عدن; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾: fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a naʿt (adjective); ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial); ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to خالدين; ﴿أَبَداً﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾: attached to the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: mubtadaʾ; ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: attached to an omitted khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position; ﴿خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من and has no grammatical position.

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنفَكِّينَ حَتَّىٰ تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ﴾.
He means [by «البينة»] the Prophet ﷺ. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "لَمْ يَكُنِ الْمُشْرِكُون وأَهْلُ الْكِتابِ مُنْفَكِّين". The tafsīr has differed: it was said: they were not to be «منفكين», [i.e.] desisting, until [145/a] the clear proof came to them.
Meaning: the sending of Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. Others said: they were not to abandon the description of Muhammad ﷺ in their Book — that he is a prophet — until he appeared; [then] they split up and differed. And that is confirmed by … [Translator's note: the sentence «ويصدّق ذلك» breaks off here in the source; presumably it continues with the next verse, ﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾ (4).]

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَسُولٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
An indefinite noun made to follow anew upon «البينة», which is definite, just as He said: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ، فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾. In the reading of Ubayy it is: "رَسُولاً مِنَ اللهِ", in the accusative, by being cut off (inqiṭāʿ) from «البيِّنة».

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلْبَيِّنَةُ﴾.
«الانفكاك» may be in the sense of يُزال (ceasing, as in «ما زال», "not cease to"), and it may be in the sense of the separation you know. When it is in the sense of يَزال, it must have a verb [after it], and a negation must be with it; so you say: ما انفككت أذكرك (I have not ceased mentioning you), meaning: ما زلت أذكرك. When it is not in the sense of يزال, you say: قد انفككت منك (I have separated from you), and انفك الشىء من الشىء (the thing came apart from the thing); so it is without a negation and without a verb. Dhū al-Rumma said:
قلائص لا تنفك إِلاّ مُناخة * على الخسف أو ترمى بلداً قفرا
(Young she-camels that never cease except made to kneel in hardship, or [else] they make for a desolate land.)
He brought only (إِلاَّ) into it while intending by it the complete [verb] [Translator's note: i.e. «تنفك» in its full sense of separating, not the defective sense of «يزال»], contrary to يزال; because you do not say: ما زلت إلا قائماً (I did not cease except standing). [Translator's note: the verse is usually cited with «حراجيج ما تنفك» and «أو نرمي بها»; translated as printed.]

farraa:5-5.t:
His words, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَآ أُمِرُوۤاْ إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُواْ ٱللَّهَ﴾.
The Arabs often put the lām in the place of (أن) with [verbs of] commanding and willing. Among that is the word of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿يُرِيدُ اللهُ لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُم﴾, and ﴿يُرِيدُونَ لِيُطْفِئُوا﴾. And concerning commanding He said in more than one place of the Revelation: ﴿وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوا اللهَ مُخْلِصِينَ"; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ذلك الدين القيمة", while in our reading it is "وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ", and it is [145/b] among the things annexed to themselves because of the difference of their two wordings. It has been explained in more than one place.

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ ٱلْبَرِيَّةِ﴾.
«البرية» is without hamza, except that some of the people of the Hijaz pronounced it with hamza, as if they took it from the word of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: «برأكم» (He created you) and «برأ الخلق» (He created creation). Whoever does not give it a hamza may also take it from this meaning; then they agreed on dropping its hamza, just as they agreed on [dropping it in] يَرَى, تَرى and نرى. If it is taken from «البَرَى», it is without hamza; «البرى» is dust. I heard the Arabs say:
بفيه البرى، وحمّى خيبرى، وشرُّ ما يرى [فإنه خيسرى]
(Dust in his mouth, and the fever of Khaybar, and the worst of what may be seen — [for he is a loser].)

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا»; «منفكيِّن» here: the khabar (predicate) of كان, from the complete (tāmm) انفكَّ; and the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «حتى تأتيهم» is attached to «منفكين».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «رسول»: badal (substitute) of {الْبَيِّنَةُ}, a substitute of the whole for the whole by way of hyperbole: He made the Messenger the very البنية [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently البينة (the clear proof) is meant]; the preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) رسول; and the clause «يتلو» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رسول».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (فيها كتب قيمة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is a naʿt (adjective) of {صُحُفًا}.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «وما تفرَّق» is conjoined to the clause {لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ}; the preposition «من بعد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تفرَّق»; «ما»: maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «وما أُمروا» is conjoined to the clause «ما تفرق»; the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليعبدوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أمروا»; «مخلصين»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «يعبدوا»; the preposition «له» is attached to «مخلصين»; «الدين»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle; «حنفاء»: a second ḥāl; and the clause «وذلك دين» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition «من أهل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا»; «خالدين»: ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the khabar (predicate) of «إنَّ»; «هم»: pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and the clause «أولئك شر» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «أولئك هم خير» is the khabar (predicate) of إنَّ, and «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition «عند» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) in «جزاؤهم»; the clause «جزاؤهم جنات» is resumptive; the clause «تجري» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), since جنات is annexed to the proper name «عدن» and so acquired definiteness; the clause «رضي الله عنهم» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «ذلك لمن خشي».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (رسول): a badal (substitute) for (البينة), or nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of «هي رسول». (يتلو) is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (رسول). In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is (رسولا), in the accusative (naṣb), as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (فيها كتب): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of (صحف).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying (مخلصين) and (حنفاء): two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the latent pronoun in (يعبدوا).
His saying (وذلك دين القيمة): (ذلك) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (دين) is the khabar (predicate) of (ذلك). (القيمة) is an adjective standing in place of an omitted qualified noun, its implied form being «دين الملة القيمة», i.e. the upright (al-mustaqīma) [religion]; and it was said: its implied form is «دين الجماعة القيمة». His saying (والمشركين), the second one, is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (الذين); and it was said: it is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ), conjoined to (أهل), like the first, for the same reason. [Translator's note: the second (والمشركين) occurs in verse 6 of this surah, though the source treats it here.]

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying (جزاؤهم عند ربهم): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (جنات) is its khabar (predicate), i.e. their reward is entering gardens; (تجري) is a naʿt (adjective) of (جنات).
His saying (خالدين): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in (جزاؤهم). That is permissible because the maṣdar (verbal noun) here does not have the meaning of «أن فعل» and «أن يفعل», so as to require that nothing separate it from what is attached to it. Separation between it and what is attached to it is only prohibited when it has the meaning of «أن فعل» and «أن يفعل», and this is not of that kind. (أبدا) is an adverb of time.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (لم يكن الذين): the nūn was given kasra because it is vowelless and the lām after it is vowelless; its origin is vowellessness for the jussive. The wāw before it was dropped because it was vowelless and the nūn was vowelless, and the wāw was not restored when the nūn took a vowel, because the vowel is incidental and not taken into account. Its like is (قم الليل), and it is frequent in the Qur'an in every jussive or indeclinable verb whose middle radical is wāw or yāʾ, or an alif replacing one of them. Dropping the nūn from (يكن) here, according to the dialect of those who say (لم يك زيد قائما), is not good, because it has taken a vowel; it may be dropped only when it is vowelless in continuous speech, so that it resembles the letters of prolongation and softness and is dropped because of the resemblance and frequent use. When it takes a vowel, the resemblance disappears and dropping is prevented, except in poetry, for its dropping has come after it took a vowel because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.
His saying (والمشركين): conjoined to (أهل). It is not good to conjoin (المشركين) to (الذين), because the meaning would be reversed and the polytheists would become part of the People of the Book, while they are not of them.
His saying (منفكين): its meaning is "separating from one another", i.e. "divided"; what indicates that is His saying (وما تفرق الذين أوتوا الكتاب). It is taken from their saying "the thing has come apart (انفك) from the thing" when it separates from it. So it needs no khabar (predicate) when it means "divided"; had it meant "ceasing" it would have needed a khabar, because it would then be one of the sisters of (كان).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يكن﴾: a deficient imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of the jussive being the sukūn.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as the noun (ism) of «يكن».
﴿كفروا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿من أهل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿الكتاب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿والمشركين﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «المشركين» is conjoined to ﴿أهل﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ.
﴿منفكين﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «يكن», accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ.
﴿حتى﴾: a particle of limit and genitive.
﴿تأتيهم﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by an «أن» concealed after «حتى», and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and the verb is genitive by «حتى», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿منفكين﴾.
﴿البيِّنة﴾: fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the overt ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿رسول﴾: a whole-for-whole badal (substitute) for ﴿البيِّنة﴾, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿من الله﴾: «من» is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a noun in the genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿رسول﴾, or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of it.
﴿يتلو﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the agent is ﴿هو﴾; the clause ﴿يتلو﴾ is a second adjective (ṣifa), or a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿صحفًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿مطهرة﴾: an adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿صحفًا﴾, accusative.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿كتب﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿قيمة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتب﴾, nominative; the clause is a second adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿صحفًا﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; «ما» is negating.
﴿تفرق﴾: a past verb.
﴿الذين﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿أوتوا﴾: a past verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿أوتوا﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين».
﴿الكتاب﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿من بعد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تفرق﴾.
﴿ما﴾: maṣdariyya.
﴿جاءتهم﴾: a past verb, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.
﴿البيِّنة﴾: a postponed fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما جاءتهم﴾ is genitive by ﴿بعد﴾ being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «ما» is negating.
﴿أمروا﴾: a past verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿ليعبدوا﴾: the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and «يعبدوا» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an «أن» concealed after the lām, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar from «أن» and the verb is genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أمروا﴾.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿مخلصين﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of ﴿يعبدوا﴾.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مخلصين﴾.
﴿الدين﴾: mafʿūl bihi of ﴿مخلصين﴾, because it is an active participle.
﴿حنفاء﴾: a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the ḥāl before it, or from the pronoun latent in it, so it is an overlapping ḥāl (mutadākhila).
﴿ويقيموا الصلاة﴾: conjoined to ﴿ليعبدوا الله﴾.
﴿ويؤتوا الزكاة﴾: likewise conjoined.
﴿وذلك﴾: the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial, and «ذا» is a demonstrative indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address.
﴿دين﴾: khabar (predicate) of «ذا», nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿القيمة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿إن الذين﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position; «إن» is an abrogating particle, and ﴿الذين﴾ is its noun (ism).
﴿كفروا﴾: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿كفروا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿من أهل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent.
﴿الكتاب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿والمشركين﴾: conjoined, genitive (majrūr).
﴿في نار﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿جهنم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿خالدين﴾: an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara) from the pronoun latent in the khabar.
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدين﴾.
﴿أولئك﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿هم﴾: a second mubtadaʾ, or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) for emphasis.
﴿شرّ﴾: khabar of «هم».
﴿البرية﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿أولئك هم شر البرية﴾ is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾, or it gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿إن الذين﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position; «إن» is an abrogating particle, and «الذين» is its noun (ism).
﴿آمنوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿وعملوا﴾: a verb and its fāʿil.
﴿الصالحات﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أولئك﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿هم﴾: a second mubtadaʾ, or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) for emphasis.
﴿خير﴾: khabar (predicate) of ﴿هم﴾.
﴿البرية﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿أولئك هم خير البرية﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «إن».

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿جزاؤهم﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿عند﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ﴿جزاؤهم﴾.
﴿ربهم﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿جنات﴾: khabar (predicate).
﴿عدن﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿تجري﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿من تحتها﴾: ﴿من تحت﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجري﴾, and ﴿ها﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿الأنهار﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative; the clause ﴿تجري من تحتها الأنهار﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿جنات﴾.
﴿خالدين﴾: a ḥāl from an omitted governing word, its implied form being: "entering it" (دخولها).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدين﴾.
﴿أبدًا﴾: an adverb of time expressing all-inclusiveness, also made accusative (manṣūb) by «خالدين».
﴿رضي﴾: a past verb.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative.
﴿عنهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رضي﴾.
﴿ورضوا عنه﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «رضوا عنه» is conjoined to ﴿رضي الله عنهم﴾; the clause ﴿رضي الله عنهم ورضوا عنه﴾ is a supplication (duʿāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, or a second khabar.
﴿ذلك﴾: mubtadaʾ.
﴿لمن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿خشي﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿ربه﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿خشي ربه﴾ is the ṣila, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
يَكُنِ is in the position of the jussive (jazm) by لم, and the mark of the jussive in it is the dropping of the ḍamma from the nūn; the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. If it is said: the nūn has received a vowel, so why was the wāw not restored [Translator's note: the text reads «فلم لأردت», evidently for «فلم لا رُدّت»]? The answer is that it is an accidental vowel, not fixed, so it is as though it did not exist. Do not rely on the view of whoever said that the wāw and the ḍamma were dropped for the jussive. And it is not permissible according to al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ to drop the nūn, according to the dialect of those who say:
لم يك زيد جالسا, because it has received a vowel (here); others permitted dropping it, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 581- ولاك اسقني إن كان ماؤك ذا فضل ("but give me to drink, if your water has a surplus").
وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ is conjoined to أهل; if it were conjoined to الذين it would be nominative. مُنْفَكِّينَ is the khabar (predicate) of يكن; there are two views on its meaning. ʿAṭāʾ said: منفكين means "ceasing" (bāriḥīn), and bariḥa and zāla follow one course.
Others said: «منفكّين» means "separating". Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning of the first view is: the disbelievers would not cease from what they were upon until the Messenger came to them and made their error clear to them. The meaning of the second view: the disbelievers would not separate except after the Messenger came to them, because they departed from what they had of the description of the Prophet ﷺ and disbelieved after the clarification. This view is more fitting in Arabic, because if منفكّين were in the sense of "ceasing" it would need a khabar; rather it is from "the thing separated (infakka) from the thing", i.e., left it, as Dhū al-Rumma said: [al-Ṭawīl] 582-
قلائص ما تنفكّ إلّا مناخة ... على الخسف أو يرمي بها بلدا قفرا
(Young she-camels that never cease [to be] except made to kneel in hardship, or he flings them toward a desolate land.)
Al-Aṣmaʿī claimed that Dhū al-Rumma erred in this. Abū Jaʿfar said: Al-Aṣmaʿī interpreted «ما تنفكّ» as "they do not cease", and the correct view is what al-Māzinī said: he said: al-Aṣmaʿī erred; «ما تنفكّ» is a complete statement, then he said إلّا مناخة as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ is a badal (substitute), and it may also be in the sense of "it is a messenger from Allah". Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: in the version (ḥarf) of Ubayy: «رسولا من الله», as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said:
The messenger is Muḥammad ﷺ. يَتْلُوا صُحُفاً مُطَهَّرَةً, he said: (it is) the Qur'an.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: Ibn Zayd said: (قيّمة means) straight, balanced.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: This indicates that (the correct one is) the second answer concerning منفكين.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
وَما أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ: among the readers are those who say: this is the lām of أن, i.e., "except that they worship Allah", and the origin of this is from al-Farrāʾ. As for the Basrans, according to them it is the lām of kay (purpose), i.e., they were commanded this in order that they worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His. حُنَفاءَ is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Qatāda said: al-ḥanīfiyya is circumcision, and the prohibition of (marrying) mothers, daughters, sisters and paternal aunts, and the rites (of pilgrimage). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (it is) the pilgrimage. Abū Jaʿfar said: The origin of this is that ḥanaf is inclining; so ḥanīf was said of one who inclines toward Islam with an inclination in which there is no flaw and no turning back. وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكاةَ وَذلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ: this is decisive evidence that Islam is word and deed. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلامُ [Āl ʿImrān: 19], and He makes clear that establishing prayer and giving zakāt are the religion of the upright (dīn al-qayyima).
Al-Farrāʾ said: in the version (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd «الدين القيّمة», and he claimed that it (دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ) is the annexation of a thing to itself. That is impossible according to the Basrans, because you only annex a thing to what you clarify it by, joining it to it; so it is impossible to clarify it by itself or join it to itself. So the implied form according to them is "the religion of the upright community (al-jamāʿa al-qayyima)", and it has been said: "the religion of the upright creed (al-milla al-qayyima)"; for this reason the feminine occurred.

nahhas-irab:6-7.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها أُولئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ (6) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أُولئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ (7): وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to أهل, and the accusative is permissible, conjoined to الذين. فِي نارِ جَهَنَّمَ is in the position of the khabar (predicate). خالِدِينَ فِيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial). أُولئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ is a khabar after a khabar, and the clause may also be the khabar of «إن», like إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ أُولئِكَ هُمْ خَيْرُ الْبَرِيَّةِ (7).
(البرية) without hamza is the reading of the community, and it is what is known in the speech of the Arabs; Nāfiʿ read it with hamza (البريئة), taking it from "Allah created (baraʾa) the creation". Whoever does not pronounce it with hamza takes it from al-barā, which is dust, and the dropping of the hamza is the original according to him. Al-bariyya is the creation, as was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAlī, from Abū Kurayb: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us: I heard al-Mukhtār ibn Fulful: I heard Anas ibn Mālik say: A man said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "O best of creation (khayr al-bariyya)", and he said: «That is Ibrāhīm ﷺ».
Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no sense in the argument of whoever argued from this verse that the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them, and the believers are superior to the angels, Allah's blessings be upon them, because the angels are among those who believe and do righteous deeds.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
جَزاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Ibn Masʿūd said: جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ is the interior of the Garden, i.e., its middle. Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ʿadana bi-l-makān when one resides in the place. خالِدِينَ فِيها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); أَبَداً is an adverb (ẓarf). رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ: (رضي) is from the verbs with wāw as third radical; the wāw was changed into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. And al-riḍā is with alif, its dual with wāw (riḍawān), and riḍwān; there is no sense in the report of whoever reported riḍayān.
ذلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ: it has been said: i.e., for whoever feared Allah in this world, in private and in public, and so performed His obligations and avoided disobeying Him.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {مِنْ أَهْلِ الكتاب}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [word], because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «كفروا».
His saying: {والمشركين}: The majority read «المشركين» with yāʾ, conjoined onto «أهل»; He divided the unbelievers into two kinds: People of the Book and polytheists. «والمشركون» was also read with wāw, conjoined onto «الذين كفروا».
His saying: {مُنفَكِّينَ}: the khabar (predicate) of «يكون». مُنْفَكِّين is an active participle of انْفَكَّ, and here it is the complete (tāmma) [verb], so it does not need a khabar. Some claimed that it is here deficient (nāqiṣa) and that the khabar is implied, its implied form being: "ceasing to know the matter of Muḥammad ﷺ". The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «Omitting the khabar of kāna [and its sisters] is not permissible, neither by restriction (iqtiṣār) nor by abbreviation (ikhtiṣār); and they made his saying:
4612 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
يَبْغي جِوارَكِ حينَ ليسَ مُجِيرُ
(…he seeks your protection when there is no protector)
i.e. "in the world", a case of poetic licence (ḍarūra).» I say: the rationale of those who prohibited it is that they said: the khabar has become required from two sides: from the side of its being what is predicated, so it is one of the two parts of the predication; and from the side of its being made accusative by the verb. This is refuted by the two objects of «ظنَّ», for each of them has the two mentioned features, and yet both — or one of them — are omitted by abbreviation; as for restriction, there is disagreement and detail on it, which has been set out in the course of this work.
His saying: {حتى تَأْتِيَهُمُ}: attached to «لم يكنْ» or to «مُنْفَكِّين».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {رَسُولٌ}: The majority read it in the nominative as a badal (substitute) from «البيِّنة»: either a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), or [a badal of] the whole for the whole by way of hyperbole, making the Messenger himself the clear proof; or by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the clear proof of a messenger. It may also be nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a messenger". ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Ubayy read «رسولاً» as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «البيِّنة», and the discussion of it is as preceded, regarding hyperbole or omission of the muḍāf.
His saying: {مِّنَ الله}: It may be attached to «رسولٌ» itself, or to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «رسول». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted a third view, namely that it is a ḥāl of «صُحُفاً», the implied form being: he recites purified pages sent down from Allah; i.e. it was originally an adjective of the indefinite noun, and when it was placed before it, it was made accusative as a ḥāl.
His saying: {يَتْلُو}: It may be an adjective of «رسول», or a ḥāl of the pronoun in the preposition [with its noun] before it, if you make that an adjective of «رسول».

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {فِيهَا كُتُبٌ}: It may be a clause that is an adjective of «صُحُفاً», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of «مُطَهَّرَة»; or the adjective or ḥāl may be the preposition and its genitive noun only, with «كُتُبٌ» as its fāʿil (agent), and this is the best.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدين}: The majority read it with kasra on the lām, as an active participle, with «الدّينَ» made accusative by it. Al-Ḥasan [read] it with fatḥa, in the sense that they themselves are made sincere in their intentions; and «الدينَ» is accusative on one of two views: either by removal of the preposition (isqāṭ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. in the religion; or as a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the sense of «ليَعْبُدوا», as though it were said: that they practise the religion, or that they worship with worship; so the latitude is either in the verb or in the maṣdar. «مُخْلِصِين» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يعبدون».
His saying: {حُنَفَآءَ}: a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl of the preceding ḥāl, i.e. of the pronoun latent in it. And His saying: {وَمَآ أمروا}, i.e. they were not commanded with what they were commanded except for such-and-such. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «وما أُمِروا إلاَّ أَنْ يَعْبُدوا», i.e. that they worship. The exposition of the like of it is at His saying {وَأُمِرْنَا لِنُسْلِمَ لِرَبِّ العالمين} [verse 71] in al-Anʿām.
And His saying: {وَذَلِكَ دِينُ القيمة}, i.e. [the religion of] the upright community or creed, i.e. the straight one. It was also said: the upright books, because they were mentioned earlier — He the Exalted said: {فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ} [al-Bayyina: 3] — so when He repeated it, He repeated it with the «أل» of prior reference, as in His saying: {فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول} [al-Muzzammil: 16]. This is good; Muḥammad ibn al-Ashʿat al-Ṭālaqānī said it. ʿAbd Allāh read: «وذلك الدِّين القيمةِ», and the feminine is then either by interpreting الدِّين as المِلّة (the creed), as in his saying:
4613 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سائِلْ بني أسدٍ ما هذه الصَوْتُ
(…ask the Banū Asad what this sound is)
by interpreting it as الصيحة (the cry); or because it is the tāʾ of intensification, as in عَلاَّمة.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {إِنَّ الذين كَفَرُواْ}: as [explained] at the beginning of the sūra. And His saying: «في نارِ» — this is the khabar (predicate), and «خالدين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun latent in the khabar.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {البرية}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn Dhakwān read «البَريئة» with a hamza in both words, and the rest with a doubled yāʾ. There is disagreement about that hamza. It was said: it is the original, from بَرَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ (Allah created the creation), i.e. He originated and invented it; so it is فعيلة in the sense of مَفْعولة, and it was only lightened, and its lightening became obligatory among the generality of the Arabs. I have mentioned that the Arabs mostly made the lightening of certain words obligatory, among them: النبيّ, الخابِية, الذُّرِّيَّة and البَرِيَّة. It was also said: rather, البَرِيَّة without hamza is derived from البَرا, which is dust, so it is an original form by itself; thus the two readings differ in origin and agree in meaning. However, Ibn ʿAṭiyya disparaged this, saying: «This derivation makes the hamza an error, and it is an unsatisfactory derivation.» End of quotation. He means that if it is said that it is derived from البَرا, which is dust, then where would [the hamza] come from in the other reading? This does not follow, because they are two independent readings, each with an independent origin: [the one] was said to be from بَرَأَ, i.e. created, and this one from البَرا, because they were created from it; and the meaning of both readings is one thing, namely the whole of creation. No attention is paid to those grammarians and readers who considered the hamza weak, because it is established by mass transmission (tawātur).
The majority read «خيرُ البَرِيَّة» as the counterpart of «شَرّ». ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd al-Wāḥid [read] «خِيارُ», which is the plural of خَيِّر, like جِياد and طِياب as plurals of جَيِّد and طَيِّب; al-Zamakhsharī said this.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {خَالِدِينَ}: a ḥāl whose governor is omitted, i.e. «دَخَلوها» or «أُعْطُوها» ("they entered it" or "they were given it"). It cannot be a ḥāl from «هم» in «جزاؤهم», lest it require separation between the maṣdar and its governed word by an outsider; though some of them allowed it, and excused it on the ground that the maṣdar here is not interpreted with a maṣdar particle. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is remote." As for «عند», it may be a ḥāl from «جزاؤهم», and it may be an adverbial for it. «أبداً» is an adverb of time, accusative by «خالدين».

His saying {رِّضِىَ الله عَنْهُمْ}: It may be a fresh supplication, or a second khabar, or a ḥāl with an implied «قد», according to those who insist on that.

His saying: {ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ}: i.e. that which was mentioned, the settled residence in Paradise with eternity and Allah's being pleased with him, is for whoever «خَشِيَ به» [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense is evidently "feared his Lord", «ربَّه»].

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَةُ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «أَهْلِ». (مُنْفَكِّينَ) is the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ». (مِنْ أَهْلِ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) in «كَفَرُوا».

ukberi-tibyan:2-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُو صُحُفًا مُطَهَّرَةً (٢) فِيهَا كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ (٣)).
The words of the Exalted (رَسُولٌ): it is a badal (substitute) for «الْبَيِّنَةُ», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).
(مِنَ اللَّهِ) may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «رَسُولٌ», or attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.
(يَتْلُو) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition phrase, or a ṣifa of (رَسُولٌ).
It is also possible for «مِنَ اللَّهِ» to be a ḥāl from «صُحُفًا», i.e. he recites purified scriptures sent down from Allah.
(فِيهَا كُتُبٌ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «صُحُف».

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَذَلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ (٥)).
(مُخْلِصِينَ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَعْبُدُوا». (حُنَفَاءَ) is another ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مُخْلِصِينَ».
The words of the Exalted (دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ): that is, of the upright creed (milla) or the upright community (umma).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أُولَئِكَ هُمْ شَرُّ الْبَرِيَّةِ (٦)).
The words of the Exalted (فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ): it is the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ».
(خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the khabar.
(الْبَرِيَّةِ) is without hamza in the widespread usage, though its origin is with hamza, from «بَرَأَ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ» (Allah created the creation), i.e. originated it. It is of the pattern «فَعِيلَة» in the sense of «مَفْعُولَة», and it is an adjective that has come to be used as a noun (ṣifa ghāliba), because the qualified noun is [not] mentioned with it. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «لِأَنَّهَا يُذْكَرُ مَعَهَا الْمَوْصُوفُ» ("because the qualified noun is mentioned with it"); the sense of ṣifa ghāliba requires "is not mentioned", so a negation seems to have dropped out. The pattern is also printed as «مُفَعْوِلَة», evidently for «مَفْعُولَة».]
It is said that whoever does not pronounce it with hamza takes it from «الْبَرَى», which is earth (dust). Some have read it with hamza, according to the original form.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَزَاؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ رَبَّهُ (٨)).
The words of the Exalted (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the governor (ʿāmil) in it is omitted, its implied form being: «ادْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ» (enter it, abiding forever), or «أُعْطَوْهَا» (they were given it). It cannot be a ḥāl from the genitive pronoun in «جَزَاؤُهُمْ», because if you said that, you would separate the maṣdar (verbal noun) from what it governs by the khabar (predicate). Some allowed it, arguing that the maṣdar here is not to be construed as «أَنْ» plus the verb; but this is far-fetched. As for «عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ», it may be an adverbial (ẓarf) for «جَزَاؤُهُمْ», or a ḥāl from it.
(أَبَدًا) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qayyima
Medinan; and it was said: the correct view is that it is Meccan.
[Translator's note: the source names the sūra «سُورَةُ اَلْقَيِّمَةِ»; it is otherwise known as Sūrat al-Bayyina.]
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ والمُشْرِكِينَ مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ البَيِّنَةُ﴾ ("those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not to be released until the clear proof came to them"): ”اَلْمُشْرِكِينَ“ is in the position of the genitive (fī mawḍiʿ jarr), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to "the People of the Book". The meaning is: "those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and among the polytheists were not…".
And His saying: ﴿مُنْفَكِّينَ حَتّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ البَيِّنَةُ﴾: that is, they were not to be released from their unbelief. The meaning of ”مُنْفَكِّينَ“ is "desisting from their unbelief".

zajjaj:2-2.t: And His saying: ﴿رَسُولٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَتْلُو﴾ ("a messenger from Allah reciting"): it is nominative on two grounds. One of them is as a badal (substitute) for ”البَيِّنَةُ“; the meaning is: "until a messenger from Allah comes to them". The second ground is as an explanation of ”البَيِّنَةُ“, [i.e.] "the clear proof is a messenger from Allah reciting purified pages", that is, purified of defilements and falsehood. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِي صُحُفٍ مُكَرَّمَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 13] ﴿مَرْفُوعَةٍ مُطَهَّرَةٍ﴾ [ʿAbasa: 14] ("in honoured pages, exalted and purified").

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿فِيها كُتُبٌ قَيِّمَةٌ﴾ ("in which are upright writings"): that is, writings without crookedness, straight, distinguishing truth from falsehood with evenness and proof.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَما تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ إلا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُمُ البَيِّنَةُ﴾ ("and those who were given the Book did not divide except after the clear proof came to them"): that is, they did not divide in their religion [Translator's note: the source reads «مِلْكِهِمْ», "their dominion", evidently for «مِلَّتِهِمْ», "their religion"] and in their unbelief in the Prophet, peace be upon him, except after they had recognised clearly that he was the one they had been promised in the Torah and the Gospel. [Translator's note: the source also reads «وكَفْرِهِمْ»; read «وكُفْرِهِمْ».]

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿وَما أُمِرُوا إلا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾ ("and they were commanded only to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion"): that is, to worship Him affirming His oneness, not worshipping any other along with Him. ﴿حُنَفاءَ﴾ ("upright"): upon the religion of Abraham and the religion of Muhammad, peace be upon him. ﴿وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ ويُؤْتُوا الزَّكاةَ﴾ ("and to establish prayer and give zakāt"): that is, to believe, along with affirming [Allah's] oneness, in the Prophet ﷺ and to establish his laws. ﴿وَذَلِكَ دِينُ القَيِّمَةِ﴾ ("and that is the religion of the upright"): that is, and that is the religion of the community (umma) that is upright in truth; so that is the religion of the straight creed (milla).

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هم شَرُّ البَرِيَّةِ﴾ ("those are the worst of creatures"): the reading is ”البَرِيَّةِ“ without the hamza. Nāfiʿ read ”اَلْبَرِيئَةِ“ with hamza, while the other readers are agreed on leaving out the hamza, just as they agreed in ”اَلنَّبِيُّ“. The original form is ”اَلْبَرِيئَةِ“, except that the hamza was lightened because of frequent use. They say: ”هَذا خَيْرُ البَرِيِّةِ“ ("this is the best of creatures"), ”شَرُّ البَرِيَّةِ“ ("the worst of creatures") and ”ما في البَرِيَّةِ مِثْلُهُ“ ("there is none like him among creatures"). Its derivation is from ”بَرَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ“ ("Allah created [baraʾa] creation"). Some said: it is possible that its derivation is from ”اَلْبَرى“, which is earth (dust). But if it were so, they would not have read ”اَلْبَرِيئَةِ“ with hamza. The usage is ”بَرَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ، يَبْرَؤُهُمْ“; no one has reported ”بَراهُمْ، يَبْرِيهِمْ“, such that its derivation could be from ”اَلبَرى“, which is earth.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾: that is, gardens of permanent residence.
